blocking.heading: When you select a technical noun
blocking.text: Put each pointer target one step from the file that has the pointer.
blocking.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 45, "step" means one pointer between two files, but lines 32 and 38 of the same file use "step" for a procedure step, so one technical noun has two items.
blocking.correction: "Put a pointer to each pointer target directly in the file that has the pointer."

blocking.heading: When you select a technical noun
blocking.text: When the user tells you that an agent did not obey a rule, do not remove that rule.
blocking.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 20, the item that an agent did not obey is "a rule", but line 65 of the same file (and step 6 of SKILL.md) gives the same item the term "an instruction".
blocking.correction: "When the user tells you that an agent did not obey an instruction, do not remove that instruction. The user wants agents to obey that instruction. You can correct the text of that instruction. You can also move that instruction."

advisory.heading: When you write a sentence
advisory.text: Examine only the rules that you add or change for these conditions.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 27, "for these conditions" can attach to "add or change" or to "Examine", so the reader cannot know which rules to examine.
advisory.correction: "For these conditions, examine only the rules that you add or change."

advisory.heading: When you select a technical noun
advisory.text: Use the level of the other condition headings.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md line 35, the technical noun "condition headings" is not in the glossary or in the base list of technical-terms.md.
advisory.correction: "Use the level of the other headings that give a condition."

advisory.heading: When you select the words and the tone
advisory.text: A rule with no condition is permitted only when it is applicable to all tasks for its file.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md, line 17 permits a rule with no condition, but line 33 tells the author to put each rule of a reference file, a `docs/agents/` file, or a file that loads in each session in a section whose heading gives a condition, so the two lines do not tell where a rule for all tasks goes.
advisory.correction: "A rule with no condition is permitted only when it is applicable to all tasks for its file. In a file that line 33 gives, put such a rule in a section whose heading gives the condition of all tasks of the file, for example "When you write or edit an Agent instruction"."

advisory.heading: When you select the text
advisory.text: Use the condition that is applicable to the smallest number of tasks.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md, line 17 tells the author to select the narrowest condition, which is not the usual work of an agent and makes a decision necessary, but neither this file nor a pointer target gives the cause.
advisory.correction: "Use the condition that is applicable to the smallest number of tasks, because the agent then reads the rule only in the tasks that make it necessary."

advisory.heading: When you select the text
advisory.text: Put each pointer target one step from the file that has the pointer.
advisory.problem: In skills/writing/agent-instructions/references/plain-language-rules.md, line 45 forbids sequences of pointers, which is not a usual limit for an agent, but neither this file nor a pointer target gives the cause.
advisory.correction: "Put each pointer target one step from the file that has the pointer, because an agent does not always read the target of a pointer in a pointer target."

confirm.action: Give the blocking findings of this report to the confirmers of its reviewer.
